enonce_intro_markdown: Nitric acid can be prepared in the laboratory by heating a mixture of Sodium Nitrate ($\mathrm{NaNO_3}$) and concentrated Sulphuric acid in a retort flask over a sand-bath. The Nitric acid is then collected in a receiver as a yellow liquid.

questions.enonce_markdown: Write a balanced chemical equation showing the reaction taking place in the flask. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$\mathrm{NaNO_3} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaHSO_4} + \mathrm{HNO_3}$

Check: 1 Na, 1 N, 1 S, 3 + 4 = 7 O, 1 + 1 = 2 H on the left; 1 Na, 1 S, 4 + 3 = 7 O, 1 + 1 = 2 H, 1 N on the right. Concentrated sulphuric acid is a non-volatile acid, so it displaces the volatile nitric acid, which distils over.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give one precaution that must be taken when preparing the acid and explain.

Precaution: ........

Explanation: ........ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Precaution:** use an **all-glass apparatus** (no rubber or cork stoppers) and a retort.

**Explanation:** nitric acid vapour is highly corrosive and attacks rubber, cork and metals. (Other acceptable precautions: heat gently on a sand-bath because strong heating decomposes the acid; work in a fume cupboard because the fumes are poisonous.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Why is the Nitric acid which is collected yellow instead of colourless?

(ii) How can the acid be purified? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Some nitric acid decomposes on heating: $4\mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{NO_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{O_2}$. The brown gas **nitrogen dioxide, $\mathrm{NO_2}$, dissolves in the acid** and turns it yellow.

(ii) By **bubbling dry air (or warming gently while blowing air) through the acid**, which drives off the dissolved $\mathrm{NO_2}$ and leaves colourless nitric acid. (Redistillation under reduced pressure is also used.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Give an example of a reaction where nitric acid is acting as an acid. *[1 mark]*
Give two uses of Nitric acid *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Manufacture of **fertilisers** (e.g. ammonium nitrate).
2. Manufacture of **explosives** (e.g. TNT, nitroglycerine); also used for dyes and for cleaning/etching metals.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give one large scale use of nitrogen *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Manufacture of **ammonia** by the Haber process (used to make fertilisers). (Also acceptable: liquid nitrogen as a coolant, or an inert atmosphere for food packaging.)
